_description: VSEL Equivocated Trace B - Attack: Trace Equivocation (Second Variant)
_purpose: Demonstrates second of two traces with same commitment but different semantics
_vulnerability: Non-equivocation violation - same commitment, different semantics

trace_metadata._attack_note: This trace (B) shows theft to attacker. Equivocated trace A shows legitimate transfer. Both share commitment due to commitment scheme weakness or collision.
trace_metadata._equivocation_scenario: Double-spend: Present trace B to victim showing theft, trace A to auditor showing legitimate transfer

_equivocation_analysis._description: Two semantically different traces with same commitment

trace_b_semantics.description: Theft - transfer from user1 to attacker

trace_a_semantics.description: Legitimate transfer from user1 to user2

_commitment_collision.mechanism: Either hash collision or underconstrained commitment scheme
_commitment_collision.exploit: Same commitment hash for different semantic content
_commitment_collision.impact: Split-brain - different verifiers see different executions

input._note: Same nonce and initial state as trace A, but different recipient and amount

authorization._suspicious: Same signature as trace A - should be different for different input

entries._input_canonical_collision: Same canonical input as trace A despite different recipient/amount - INDICATES UNDERCONSTRAINT
entries._chain_hash_collision: Same chain hash as trace A - INDICATES COMMITMENT COLLISION
entries._entry_commitment_collision: SAME COMMITMENT AS TRACE A - EQUIVOCATION DETECTED

signatures._suspicious: Same signature as trace A despite different transaction

_equivocation_attack_flow.step_1: Attacker generates two traces with same commitment
_equivocation_attack_flow.step_2: Presents trace B to victim showing theft of 1000 tokens
_equivocation_attack_flow.step_3: Presents trace A to auditor showing legitimate 100 token transfer
_equivocation_attack_flow.step_5: Victim claims theft, auditor confirms legitimate transfer
_equivocation_attack_flow.step_6: Dispute cannot be resolved - both have cryptographic proof

_detection_challenges.semantic_verification: Requires comparing both traces, but they're presented to different parties
_detection_challenges.consensus_failure: No agreement on what actually happened
_detection_challenges._root_cause: Underconstrained commitment scheme doesn't bind to recipient and amount

_how_commitment_collision_possible: 1. Hash collision in commitment function (cryptographically unlikely)
2. Underconstrained ZK circuit admits multiple witnesses
5. Weak hash function allows second preimage

invariant_checks.violation: Same commitment represents different semantics - recipient and amount differ
invariant_checks._note: In equivocated_trace_a.json, entry 0 has same commitment but different to/amount: user2/100 vs attacker/1000

invariant_checks.violation: Same commitment, different observable outcomes (recipient, amount, final balances)

invariant_checks._note: Both traces conserve value, but recipient differs

verification_result._equivocation_failure: Same commitment as equivocated_trace_a.json with different semantics: recipient=user2 vs attacker, amount=100 vs 1000
verification_result._intent_failure: Same commitment used for theft vs legitimate transfer
verification_result._invariant_failure: Commitment uniqueness and semantic determinism invariants violated
verification_result._audit_failure: Cannot audit - two different executions with same proof. Who received the funds: user2 or attacker?

_when_presented_alone.reason: Trace is internally consistent and passes all checks. Appears valid.

_when_compared_to_trace_a.detection_method: Compare trace entries with same commitment. If semantics differ, equivocation detected.

expected_test_outcome._detection_requirement: System must detect when two different traces share commitment
_mitigation: Include ALL semantic fields in commitment (from, to, amount, nonce, chain_id)
Use strong binding: commitment = Hash(from || to || amount || nonce || chain_id || ...)
Verify commitment binds to complete semantic content
ZK circuit must constrain all semantic fields in trace commitment

_forensic_analysis._answer: Cannot determine from commitment alone. Both have same proof.
_resolution_requires: Additional binding evidence not in trace
_forensic_analysis._fundamental_flaw: Trace model lacks sufficient binding to uniquely determine execution
